title: Developer Toolkit Acceleration — Initiative Cadence & Evidence Log
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Purpose: establish a repeatable cadence and single-source evidence log for the Developer Toolkit Acceleration initiative. This ticket captures the weekly operating rhythm (planning -> experiment -> measurement -> retro) and the artifacts we need to prove lift for SDK adoption, docs engagement, and quickstart time-to-first-success. The aim is to reduce friction for first-time integrators and to generate defensible signals for downstream Dedicated/Private upsell.

Scope: define cadence, publish meeting templates, instrument metrics pipeline for cohort attribution, collect artifacts (PRs, Confluence playbooks, sample app telemetry), and run two 6-week cohort experiments with partner product teams.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly cadence (agenda + owner) published in Confluence and added to team calendar
Evidence ledger contains at least 12 unique artifacts (PRs, sample apps, dashboard snapshots) tagged to the initiative
Two cohort experiments launched with tracking enabled (cohort_id parameter in quickstart flow)
Key metrics pipeline validates: time-to-first-success, SDK install-to-call rate, docs dropoff at step 3
Rollups for initiative OKRs available in Looker/Grafana and shown in the monthly PM review

notes: Decision: prioritize instrumented quickstarts that run locally (no cloud creds) — reduces adoption friction for security-conscious teams.
Trade-off: delaying deep server-side eventing reduces early metric fidelity but speeds experiment start by ~3 weeks.
Suggested owner rotation: rotate demo lead each week between Eng, Docs, and PM to keep cross-functional visibility.
Slack channel: #devx-accel (pinned: cadence doc, evidence ledger link, PR checklist).
Post-mortem plan: after two cohorts, we'll run a learning retro and decide on expanding to Ruby/Go SDKs based on adoption lift and support cost.
Customer quote to monitor: 'time to first successful call' — treat reduction as success leading indicator for retention and paid conversion.
